title: How It Works - Orbital Temple
heading: How It Works
intro: The Orbital Temple project consists of three interconnected elements that work together to send names to the temple in space.
paragraph1: Once launched, the satellite will orbit Earth at an altitude of about 500 to 560 km, carrying in its memory the more than 19,000 names already sent. Ground stations will then communicate with the satellite during its passes, transmitting the new names that people submit through the website.
paragraph2: The more than 19,000 names sent so far are already in the satellite's memory, and everyone who sent one will receive a confirmation once it is in orbit. New names join a queue and are transmitted by our ground station during the satellite's passes. You'll receive an email confirmation when yours has been uploaded to the Orbital Temple.
paragraph3: On January 12, 2026, the first satellite flew aboard ISRO's PSLV-C62. The rocket reached space but failed to deploy its payload. A second satellite is now cleared to fly on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission, scheduled for Thursday, October 1, 2026.
